Henrik Weber serves as the Plant Head at Northbridge Cycles [^r1]. In this executive capacity, he acts as the approving authority for operational procurement governance [^r1]. As of 26 October 2026, his formal sign-off establishes the current operational rules governing purchasing across the facility [^r1].

## Responsibilities

Henrik Weber holds operational oversight of the manufacturing plant as Plant Head [^r1]. In this role, he authorized and approved version 4.1 of [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001 Purchase Policy]] on 2026-04-01 [^r1].

SUMMARY: Rules and Ledgerline verification requirements for supplier UN 38.3 lithium-cell transport safety certificates under purchasing policy.
INFOBOX:
Topic: UN 38.3 Certificates
Applies to: Suppliers of lithium-cell parts
Policy reference: POL-PUR-001 §6
System enforcement: Ledgerline order blocking
Status: Current
CONFLICTS:
- none
BODY:
UN 38.3 certificates verify lithium-cell transport safety compliance for parts procured by Northbridge Cycles [^r1]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]], suppliers providing lithium-cell items must maintain an active, verified certificate in Ledgerline before purchase orders can be issued [^r1]. As of 26 October 2026, an expired certificate is treated as completely absent, blocking order creation [^r1][^r2].

## Requirements and Ledgerline verification

Suppliers providing lithium-cell parts—including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any inventory items marked with `cell_safety = 1`—must have a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline before any orders can be placed [^r1]. Under POL-PUR-001 §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as having no certificate in Ledgerline [^r2].

SUMMARY: Approval threshold matrix defining purchasing approval limits evaluated on gross order value including VAT and mandating escalation routes.
INFOBOX:
Document code: POL-APR-002
Title: Approval Matrix for Purchasing
Status: current
Evaluated on: Gross order value (including VAT)
Enforced by: POL-PUR-001
CONFLICTS:
- none
BODY:
POL-APR-002 sets out the approval limits and escalation hierarchy for purchasing commitments at Northbridge Cycles [^r1][^r2]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]], all approval thresholds in this matrix are evaluated against the gross order value inclusive of VAT rather than the net basic cost [^r1]. Users are strictly prohibited from approving purchase orders they raised themselves, requiring escalation to higher authority whenever an order exceeds their delegation limit or requires independent sign-off [^r2].

## Clauses

### 1. Valuation Basis
Approval limits established in POL-APR-002 are evaluated on the gross order value, including applicable VAT, rather than net basic cost [^r1].

### 2. Self-Approval and Escalation
Users cannot self-approve orders they have raised regardless of their individual approval limit [^r2]. Any order exceeding a user's delegated authority must escalate to the next approver whose limit covers the total gross value [^r2].

Tax codes in Ledgerline classify VAT treatment across orders and purchase invoices based on supplier jurisdiction [^r1]. Domestic transactions use dedicated standard tax identifiers, whereas imports and cross-border purchases require specific reverse-charge treatment [^r1]. Correct application ensures accurate accounting according to [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001 Purchase Policy]] [^r1].

## What it holds
The tax code reference defines the VAT classification rules applied to purchase orders and invoices in Ledgerline [^r1]. It distinguishes between UK domestic VAT rates and reverse-charge regimes for foreign suppliers [^r1].

## Columns
* **Tax Code Suffix**: Identifies the regional tax classification applied in Ledgerline (`-UK` or `-RC`) [^r1].
* **Supplier Type**: Indicates whether the supplier is based in the UK or overseas [^r1].
* **Application**: Specifies the designated use across purchase orders and invoices [^r1].

## How to look up a row
Determine the location of the vendor; orders and invoices for UK suppliers use VAT codes ending in `-UK`, while overseas suppliers use reverse-charge VAT codes ending in `-RC` [^r1].

## Size
Two primary VAT code category suffixes (`-UK` and `-RC`) applied across Ledgerline orders and invoices [^r1].

POL-PUR-001 sets mandatory purchasing rules for all operations at the Manchester and Leeds sites using Ledgerline ERP [^r3]. Effective from 2026-04-01 under version 4.1, it governs purchase requisitions, approval limits, cost centre validation, and supplier qualifications [^r1]. It strictly mandates verified UN 38.3 certificates for lithium-cell components and enforces a 2% price variance cap against active rate contracts [^r2][^r16][^r20].

| Attribute | Details |
|---|---|
| Document Code | POL-PUR-001 [^r1] |
| Version | 4.1 [^r1] |
| Effective Date | 2026-04-01 [^r1] |
| Author | D. Okafor [^r1] |
| Approver | [[user-hweber|Henrik Weber]] [^r1] |
| Scope | Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01), Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) [^r3] |
| Status | Current [^r1] |

## Clauses

### 2. Scope
The purchase policy applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) through Ledgerline ERP [^r3].

### 3. Requests before orders
Every purchase must start with a purchase request in Ledgerline, unless it qualifies as a direct order under section 3.3 [^r4]. A purchase request specifies the item, quantity, need-by date, warehouse, and the cost centre bearing the expenditure [^r5]. A direct purchase order without a prior request is permitted only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less [^r6]. A purchase order created against a purchase request is not permitted to exceed the requested quantity [^r7].

### 4. Cost centres and budgets
Every purchase request and order must be charged to an open cost centre [^r8]. Ledgerline automatically saves any order booked against a closed cost centre as a Draft, and Draft orders are never sent to suppliers [^r9]. Staff must check cost centre status in Ledgerline using screen [[screen-fin-cc-01|FIN-CC-01]] or verify with Finance before raising an order [^r10].

### 5. Approval limits
Approval limits are evaluated against the gross value including VAT rather than the basic net value [^r11]. If an order exceeds the raiser's personal limit in the approval matrix ([[pol-apr-002|POL-APR-002]]), it must be approved by the next person up the line whose authority covers it [^r12]. Self-approval of purchase orders is strictly prohibited under all circumstances [^r13]. Approval of a purchase request covers the resulting purchase order provided the approver's personal limit covers the order's gross value [^r14].

### 6. Supplier qualification
Purchase orders may only be placed with suppliers that are active in the supplier master [^r15]. Lithium-cell parts (including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any item with cell_safety = 1) may only be purchased from suppliers holding a verified, unexpired [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] in Ledgerline [^r2][^r16]. Before placing orders with a new supplier, the supplier must be formally onboarded under POL-SUP-003 [^r17]. Purchasers must prefer suppliers with current rate contracts, and a cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part [^r18].

### 7. Prices
Orders must apply rates from current rate contracts, treating historical order prices as reference only [^r19]. Any purchase order placed at a price more than 2% above the rate contract requires written justification from the manager in the order remarks [^r2][^r20].

### 8. Tax
UK suppliers are charged UK VAT using [[data-tax-codes|tax codes]] ending in -UK, whereas non-UK suppliers are charged VAT via reverse charge using tax codes ending in -RC [^r21].

### 9. Records
An order must carry an official Ledgerline document number and attain Released status before the supplier is instructed to deliver or the requester is told the order is placed [^r22].

## Versions and conflicts
- Price tolerance over rate contract: Under version 4.1 (effective 2026-04-01), the allowed price tolerance is 2% with written justification in order remarks [^r2][^r20]. Previously, the tolerance threshold was 5% [^r2]. Kind: superseded.
